idea: How to maintain a water tank
title: Water Tank Maintenance: Sediment Flushes
description: A practical educational lesson demonstrating how water tank sediment isolation works and why routine bottom flushing prevents pipe blockages.
image_prompt: A realistic educational vertical cutaway view showing the lower section of a dark blue polyethylene water storage tank installed on a clean concrete pad outdoors. Inside the tank, clear water reveals a distinct layer of fine brown sediment settled flat along the very bottom surface. A supply outlet pipe fitted with a PVC ball valve penetrates the tank wall 10 centimeters above the floor, safely drawing clear water above the sediment layer. At the lowest point of the tank base, a separate scour drain pipe with a red handle ball valve is shown, showing the correct plumbing layout for cleaning out sludge. Professional plumbing photography style, sharp focus on fittings and tank floor, clean natural light, realistic pipe geometry, 9:16 vertical composition. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no graphical arrows or text panels.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway cross-section of a water tank base to highlight the vertical separation between the supply outlet and the drain valve. Viewers can see how mineral sediment naturally drops to the tank floor over time. By placing the primary supply pipe slightly above the tank floor and a dedicated drain pipe at the bottom, sediment remains trapped below the supply line until flushed.

on_image_text.hook: Prevent Tank Sludge From Clogging Household Pipes
on_image_text.explanation: Supply pipes draw clean water above the floor while sediment settles to the bottom.
on_image_text.callout: Raised Outlet vs. Bottom Scour Valve
on_image_text.takeaway: Open the bottom scour valve every 6 months to flush out settled debris.
